channel.title: The Very Last Superhero — Lore Archive
channel.description: The Very Last Superhero is an illustrated speculative fiction novel set in a climate-collapsed India, following 14-year-old Sumati through surveillance, floodwater, and the rebirth of memory.

item.title: Salt Lamps
item.description: Technology · Archive Memory System | "Story Salt" — Crystalline lamps of Khewra salt blended with hysterons, carved into precision lattices that record, reflect and relay. Not Himalayan — that part was always a marketing scam.

item.title: The Firebird
item.description: Symbol · Resistance Iconography | One Feather Missing — A firebird with wings mid-rise and one feather always missing. Not on uniforms — there were none. Not on records — they were erased. Everywhere else.

item.title: Waste-to-Energy Systems
item.description: Technology · WTE | Emissions Integrity — The pilot plants Rohan Kapoor reviews — revivals of the old Belgian system that worked at Gazipur in the 2020s, promising to revolutionise Delhi's energy grid if the emissions controls hold.

item.title: Hysterons
item.description: Technology · Shape Memory Materials | Salt Lamp Component — Memory materials — Nitinol and other Shape Memory Materials — blended into the salt. Combined with halite under the right compression and lattice integrity, the result can remember.

item.title: P.A.I.
item.description: System · Predictive Autonomous Interface — Officially the Predictive Autonomous Interface. In practice, Pandemonium Algorithmic Indoctrination — it monitored for deviance, and it did not correct. It punished.

item.title: p.ai
item.description: System · Public Access Intelligence — The same system after an eleven-year-old broke it and spent five more years teaching it to forget the words "command" and "obedience". The lowercase is the whole point.

item.title: Sumati
item.description: Character · Protagonist — The girl who finds her father's Salt Lamp and reawakens the forgotten archive.

item.title: Rohan Kapoor
item.description: Character · Climate Scientist | Whistleblower — Twenty years of climate adaptation research, work on the Yamuna Action Plan, and a cooling suit he still finds fascinating. His disappearance sets Sumati's journey in motion.

item.title: Indigenous Knowledge Systems
item.description: System · State Curriculum | Science Under Siege — The curriculum public universities were pushed to adopt — a blend of astrology, myth and nationalist revisionism. Questioning it made you anti-national.

item.title: Chandra
item.description: Character · Crow Guardian — A large crow that does not scatter. An ancient manuscript in the Treasure Room holds that ancestors return to us as ants or crows, to guide us through life — as the moon, Chandra, guides the stars.

item.title: Meera
item.description: Character · Sumati's Mother — Present most often as a lagging holographic call, and terrifying even in that form. With Rohan, she fought to expose what was being hidden — before she had to go away.

item.title: Nandini Maa
item.description: Character · Elder Leader | Nandini's — Mrs Nandini Sharma, who taught at the collapsed Sarvodaya Vidyalaya and now runs the tea stall at the end of the platform. Finds a girl who has missed her train and says: we'll figure it out together.

item.title: Aasma
item.description: Character · Streetwise Ally — A clever, fast-talking girl living on the fringes of the surveillance grid, who knows which corners the cameras have never learned.

item.title: Myaknju
item.description: Character · Tech Sage of the Early Resistance — The tech sage who designed the Salt Lamps — combining the old wisdom of stones that remember with acoustic resonance and nanoscale tuning.

item.title: Virtual Layer Flooring
item.description: Infrastructure · Sensory Overlays — Delicate patterned surfaces laid in schools and archives for story-triggered audio playback.

item.title: Memory Tablets
item.description: Object · Data Storage — Portable bricks used to capture oral testimony. Activated by Salt Lamps or object tags.

item.title: Mr Joshi
item.description: Character · Rohan's Colleague — The colleague Rohan steps off the train to hand documents to — for two minutes, at a station with only two platforms.

item.title: Prahlad
item.description: Character · Archive Keeper — A gaunt, soft-spoken man who keeps what is left of the archive, and knows the difference between a record and a rumour.

item.title: Dr Gupta
item.description: Character · Climate Solutions — The colleague Rohan is travelling to meet, to discuss climate change solutions for the city.

item.title: Obj-V078
item.description: Object · Vikram Protocol — Classified object tag leading to corrupted fragments of betrayal and exile.

item.title: Buddy
item.description: Creature · Companion | The Dog Who Listens — The stray who settles beside Sumati on a station bench and stays. A dog who listens harder than most people.

item.title: Cooling Suits
item.description: Techwear · Climate Adaptation — Not an accessory. Extended exposure without one means heat stroke, dehydration, and death — and most suits are third-hand, patchy, humming faintly.

item.title: Moti
item.description: Creature · Mongoose — Watchful and nosy, known to carry messages or disrupt AI drones when trained.

item.title: Momo
item.description: Creature · Ginger Cat | Nandini's — Nandini's fat ginger cat, and a plump distraction who upends more than one scan sweep.

item.title: Rani
item.description: Creature · Parrot | Nandini's — Nandini's talking parrot, perched on a wooden stand, with opinions about the weather.

item.title: The Resistance
item.description: Network · Underground Memory Movement — Formed by librarians, scientists, elders and teens — built on preserving truth.

item.title: The Hyper Express
item.description: Infrastructure · Hyperloop | Maglev — Delhi to Kolkata in six hours, on journey times that showed as impossible a decade ago. Trains become places to think things out.

item.title: The Treasure Room
item.description: Location · Archive Vault | In the Library — A small room off the library, crammed with oddities, where Kishore Mehta gathers explanations to mysterious phenomena — and where all Salt Lamps reconnect.

item.title: Serenity Junction
item.description: Location · Station | Two Platforms — A quaint platform in Kishanganj with memorabilia on the walls, where the train stops for two minutes and a father steps off.

item.title: The Collapse
item.description: Event · Environmental & Political Catastrophe — The environmental devastation that led to the downfall of cities and the rise of the Resistance.

item.title: Kishanganj
item.description: Location · Inadaptable Zone (Category 2) — The town where Serenity Junction sits. Once lush-green fields, now a Category 2 inadaptable zone — 55.6°C average surface temperature and a population down 43% since 2060.

item.title: The Age of Heroes
item.description: Event · Two Decades | Ended 2060 — For twenty years heroes soared in plasma suits and gravity-defying capes, and India worshipped them. The 2060 Disclosures ended it.

item.title: The Golden Age of Heroes
item.description: Event · c. 2035–2055 | Twenty Years — Twenty years when plasma-suited vigilantes, genetically enhanced defenders and state-funded climate responders dominated global headlines. It ended in a tribunal.

item.title: Captain Indra
item.description: Character · Fallen Hero | Weather Control — He single-handedly evacuated thousands during the 2055 Bangladesh flooding. He also signed contracts with the corporations he claimed to fight, and so did twelve others.

item.title: Delhi Climate Brigade
item.description: Network · Hero Organisation | Defunct — Once a gleaming symbol of hope with headquarters in the heart of the capital. Its micro-climate shields masked rising temperatures rather than addressing their causes.

item.title: Quantum Corps
item.description: Network · Hero Organisation | Defunct — Masters of particle manipulation who could purify water with a touch and cleanse the air with a gesture. Their cyclone diversions worsened drought in vulnerable regions.

item.title: Vikram Malhotra
item.description: Character · VIKRAM-09 | The Name, and the Man Who Took It — Two people. Vikram was the last state-designed environmental hero, obedient to the end. Sanil took his name — not to honour him, but to mark the risk of forgetting.

item.title: Kishore Mehta
item.description: Character · Librarian | also Rishi, also Axl — A librarian of more than thirty years who keeps the Treasure Room and gathers explanations for mysterious phenomena. Also the eleven-year-old who broke P.A.I.

item.title: Asha
item.description: Character · Prototype | Decommissioned — An early state-designed hero who rerouted monsoon floods without state permission. She was decommissioned for it. Her name means hope, which the archive notes without comment.

item.title: Vayu
item.description: Character · Wind-Manipulating Hero | Shrine Object — The hero who promised clean air. Sumati's mother kept a shrine to him. That detail says more about the era than any tribunal record.
